justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: real-time decisions via Scoring Engine Container (R-01), analyst review workflows via Case Management API Container (R-02), and zero-downtime model updates via Model Loader & Verifier Component using atomic pointer swapping (R-03).
justifications.performance_efficiency: Sub-50ms P99 at 3,000 rps is achieved through in-memory evaluation in Model Evaluator Component, sub-millisecond lookups via Amazon ElastiCache Serverless, and asynchronous decoupling of audit ingestion through Amazon SQS & DLQ.
justifications.compatibility: The architecture integrates cleanly with external systems using standard protocols: mTLS/gRPC for Payment Gateway, OIDC/SAML for Corporate IdP, and standard APIs for Card Networks / Tokenization Service and AWS KMS.
justifications.usability: While Fraud Analysts and Compliance Officers are served by Case Management API Controller and Compliance API Controller, the architecture lacks any web UI or user-facing frontend container for conducting manual case reviews.
justifications.reliability: R-07 availability is addressed through Circuit Breaker Controller in Envoy Proxy, in-memory Local Heuristic Fallback Component during timeouts or errors, and dead-letter queue resilience in Amazon SQS & DLQ.
justifications.security: Strong security is established via TLS 1.3, IdP integration, and tamper-evident logging in AWS QLDB. However, explicit data masking or redaction mechanisms within Case Management API Container preventing analysts from viewing PAN are missing.
justifications.maintainability: The system features modular microservices (Scoring Engine Container, Case Management API Container, Audit & Compliance Ledger Container) with clear boundaries, asynchronous decoupling, and minimal operational complexity suitable for a three-engineer team.
justifications.portability: Although compute workloads run in portable containers, the architecture has tight architectural coupling to proprietary AWS-managed services, specifically AWS QLDB, Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, and Amazon SQS.

PERF-01.justification: In-memory Go model execution, sub-millisecond Redis feature caching, and asynchronous SQS audit publishing keep the evaluation path well under the 50 ms P99 latency threshold.
tradeoffs: In-memory models reduce latency but consume more host RAM

PERF-02.justification: Scoring and case review are decoupled across separate containers and data stores. Analyst workloads query PostgreSQL read replicas, completely isolating operational DB traffic from real-time scoring.
sensitivity_points: Aurora replication lag for newly created review cases
tradeoffs: Read replicas increase AWS monthly cost to guarantee scoring isolation

AVAIL-01.justification: Envoy circuit breakers and the local heuristic fallback component provide rapid degraded scoring without blocking requests. However, behavior during a total scoring container crash requires explicit fail-open upstream configuration.
sensitivity_points: Circuit breaker trip thresholds and timeout sensitivities
tradeoffs: Heuristic fallback maintains availability but slightly increases false approval risk

AVAIL-02.justification: The scoring engine publishes audit events asynchronously to SQS with DLQ backing. QLDB slowdowns or outages do not backpressure real-time scoring or cause audit data loss.
sensitivity_points: SQS retention limits during prolonged ledger outages
tradeoffs: Asynchronous buffering guarantees low scoring latency but delays ledger write consistency

MOD-01.justification: The Model Loader & Verifier background worker verifies artifacts and performs zero-downtime atomic pointer swaps in memory, tagging every output decision with the active model version.
sensitivity_points: Atomic memory pointer updates across Go runtime routines
tradeoffs: Holding previous and new models concurrently in memory increases memory footprint

MOD-02.justification: Dynamic rule loading and Redis velocity lookups support updating rule evaluation without downtime. However, the exact publishing pipeline between Case Management and Scoring Engine is partially unmodeled.
sensitivity_points: Cache propagation delay across distributed Redis nodes
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule injection adds runtime parsing overhead compared to static compilation

SEC-01.justification: External tokenization and IdP access controls prevent analysts from seeing clear-text card data. However, the architecture defines no SIEM, IDS, or anomalous access alerting mechanism for 15-minute response.
sensitivity_points: Absence of dedicated security log monitoring and alert tooling
tradeoffs: Omitting a dedicated SIEM service saves budget but impedes automated breach alerting

SEC-02.justification: AWS QLDB provides an append-only, cryptographically verifiable ledger retaining Ion document revisions. The Compliance API and Tamper-Evident Journal Manager allow rapid retrieval of historical inputs and model versions.
sensitivity_points: Retention policy enforcement in QLDB journal storage
tradeoffs: Immutable ledger storage increases long-term storage costs over 7 years
